version.changelog: Video creation in React - comprehensive patterns and best practices

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: remotion
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle contains documentation and example React/Remotion components for video creation. It includes standard package installation commands (e.g., `npx remotion add @remotion/three`) and examples of fetching remote resources from legitimate domains (e.g., `lottiefiles.com`, `remotion.media`) or user-provided URLs. There is no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, persistence, obfuscation, or prompt injection against the agent beyond its stated purpose of providing Remotion best practices.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent Remotion guidance, but it repeatedly tells agents to run unpinned package-manager commands and includes an arbitrary URL-fetching metadata example without security scoping.

dimensions.detail: Remote media and fetch examples are normal for Remotion projects, but the artifact does not consistently warn about trusted origins, request metadata, or server-side network exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Multiple rule files instruct use of npx, bunx, yarn, or pnpm exec to add Remotion packages without pinned versions or lockfile/provenance guidance, so following the instructions can execute mutable registry-resolved code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger says to use the skill whenever dealing with Remotion code, which is broad but still aligned to the skill domain and does not attempt to override unrelated agent policy.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No artifact-backed evidence of persistence, privilege escalation, credential handling, background workers, memory writes, or hidden post-install behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Remotion best-practices guidance, and most files are ordinary Markdown examples, but a best-practices skill recommending fetch(props.dataUrl) before rendering without validation or trust boundaries can lead users to copy an SSRF-prone pattern in server-side render workflows.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing or using this skill in agent-assisted coding. Prefer pinned Remotion package versions and lockfile-controlled installs, and do not copy the arbitrary dataUrl fetch pattern into render services that accept untrusted props unless you add URL allowlisting, timeouts, response limits, and network egress controls.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad Remotion-code trigger is real, but it stays within the Remotion domain and is not an instruction hijack by itself.
[RP1] expected: The unpinned package-runner commands are present across several prerequisite sections and are purpose-aligned, but they are a material supply-chain concern because an agent may execute mutable package code.
[E1] expected: The example fetch to api.example.com is a normal placeholder for dynamic metadata and not evidence of exfiltration from the skill itself.
[EA4] expected: The GIF loop example describes playback behavior, not an unbounded agent loop or background resource consumer.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote audio/media and data fetching are expected in Remotion examples, but the lack of trust-origin guidance is a real caution for sensitive environments.
[T08] expected: Static scan correctly identified repeated unpinned package-runner commands; this supports Review rather than malicious classification because the packages are official-looking Remotion dependencies and the behavior is disclosed.
[T09] unexpected: The unrestricted fetch(props.dataUrl) metadata example is not appropriate best-practice guidance without validation, allowlisting, size limits, or notes about server-side rendering risk.
